title: Sorry, I won't be walking the runway this year
summary: Announce, very seriously, that you won't be walking the big fashion show this year, then give a tiny, everyday excuse. AI writes the excuses.
why: A TikTok trend report published October 21, 2026 lists this in its October roundup: creators apologize for not walking a famous fashion show runway, then give a mundane or oddly specific reason, like being at a pumpkin patch every Sunday in October.
steps: Think about what fills your calendar right now: a hobby, a chore, a seasonal outing or your pet.
Paste the main prompt into the AI and pick the excuse that makes you laugh most.
Film a short clip of you doing that exact thing, with the apology as on-screen text first and the excuse second.
Keep a straight face. The joke is how seriously you take it.

prompts.label: Main prompt
prompts.text: I'm making a funny TikTok. The on-screen text starts: "Sorry, I won't be walking the big fashion show runway this year." Then I give a very ordinary, oddly specific reason. My life right now includes: [for example: soccer practice drop-offs, raking leaves and a sourdough starter]. Write 10 short excuses, each under 15 words, that sound polite and official but are clearly about everyday life. Make a few of them about fall. Don't name any real people, shows or brands.

prompts.label: Variation: pet version
prompts.text: Write 8 excuses from my pet's point of view for why it won't be walking the big fashion show runway this year. My pet is a [type of pet, for example: lazy orange cat] who loves [for example: the sunny spot on the couch]. Each excuse is under 15 words and sounds like a formal statement. Add 3 short captions to go with the video.

prompts.label: Variation: small business
prompts.text: I run a [type of business, for example: bakery in a small town]. Write 8 excuses for why my team won't be walking the big fashion show runway this year, each about real, honest work we're busy with this season, like [for example: Thanksgiving pie orders]. Under 15 words each. Keep it playful. No made-up discounts, prices, customer numbers or claims. Add a short caption with a friendly invite to visit.

tips: Film the excuse, not the runway. A shot of you up to your elbows in leaves is funnier than any fashion shot.
Use a formal font or a press-release style for the apology line, then plain text for the excuse.
Leave out the name of any real fashion show or brand. "The big fashion show" gets the joke across.
Short, specific excuses beat long ones. "Every Sunday in October" is better than "I'm busy".
